experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds up close against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with iconic savannah landscapes and diverse birdlife.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Safari
experiences.description: Explore Lake Nakuru National Park, home to thousands of pink flamingos that paint the lake shores in vivid color. The park is also a sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and over 450 bird species, making it a compact but incredibly diverse wildlife destination.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the rich traditions of the Maasai people with an authentic village visit. Participate in traditional dances, learn about ancient warrior customs, visit local homesteads called manyattas, and shop for handcrafted beaded jewelry directly from artisans while gaining deep cultural insight into one of Africa's most iconic tribes.
experiences.location: Maasai Villages near Maasai Mara, Narok County

experiences.name: Aberdare Forest Night Game Drive & Treetop Lodge
experiences.description: Experience the magic of Kenya's highland rainforest with a nocturnal game drive through the Aberdare National Park. Spot elusive forest elephants, giant forest hogs, bongos, and leopards by spotlight. Staying at a treetop lodge over a waterhole allows you to watch wildlife gather through the night in a truly unique setting.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a shared shuttle or matatu (local minibus) transfer toward Narok County. The journey to Maasai Mara takes approximately 5–6 hours. Enjoy the scenic Rift Valley views along the way. Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve by early evening and check in.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your accommodation, freshen up, and take a short orientation walk around the lodge grounds. Meet fellow travelers and staff to get tips on budget-friendly activities. Enjoy the warm July evening air (around 18–20°C at night) and watch the sunset over the savannah from the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport — grab a light snack or packed meal from a budget café at JKIA (around KES 300–500).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple roadside lunch during the transfer stop in Narok town — try a local 'nyama choma' (roasted meat) joint or a chapati and beans meal for around KES 200–350.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique stay or a nearby budget-friendly lodge restaurant. Ask for the set menu or 'daily special' — typically ugali, sukuma wiki (collard greens), and stewed meat for around KES 600–900.

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle or matatu transfer in advance from Nairobi to save costs (approx. KES 1,500–2,500 one way). Carry enough Kenyan shillings as ATMs are scarce near the Mara. Stay hydrated during the long road journey.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning budget game drive inside Maasai Mara National Reserve. Arrange a shared game drive vehicle through your lodge or a local budget operator to split costs (approx. KES 3,000–5,000 per person for a shared 4x4). Depart by 06:30 to catch wildlife at peak activity. Look for lions, elephants, zebras, and giraffes in the golden morning light. July is an excellent time as the Great Wildebeest Migration begins moving into the Mara from the Serengeti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by midday. Rest during the hottest part of the day (up to 25°C). Visit the nearby Maasai village (cultural visit fee approx. KES 500–800 per person) to learn about traditional Maasai lifestyle, beadwork, and customs. This is a budget-friendly, enriching experience that supports the local community.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the lodge perimeter with a guide (often complimentary or low-cost through your accommodation). Watch for hippos near the Mara River at dusk. Gather around a communal campfire at the lodge, share stories with other travelers, and stargaze in the clear July sky.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-drive breakfast at the lodge — packed tea/coffee, boiled eggs, and bread (included or KES 400–600 if extra).
meals.lunch: Simple lodge lunch or self-catered — carry packed snacks (bananas, mandazi pastries, groundnuts) bought from Narok town to save money.
meals.dinner: Budget set dinner at the lodge or a nearby tented camp's communal dining area — ugali with beef stew or vegetable curry, around KES 700–1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Always book shared game drives rather than private ones to significantly reduce costs. Bring a light jacket for early morning drives as temperatures can drop to 14–16°C before sunrise. Apply sunscreen for the afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive focusing on the Mara River area — the iconic crossing point of the Great Wildebeest Migration. Depart by 06:00 with your shared game drive group. Position near the river to potentially witness wildebeest and zebra crossing, braving crocodiles and strong currents. This is one of the world's greatest wildlife spectacles and peaks in July–August.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the open savannah plains. Search for the 'Big Five' — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. The afternoon light is excellent for photography. Look for cheetahs on termite mounds scanning for prey. Return to the lodge by 17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge. Join a free or low-cost guided bush walk if offered by your accommodation. Enjoy the sounds of the African bush — hyenas calling, nightjars singing, and distant lion roars. Wind down with a cup of Kenyan chai (tea) on the lodge veranda.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the lodge — thermos of tea, sandwiches, and fruit (KES 400–600 or included).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten in the vehicle or at a designated picnic site inside the reserve — self-catered with bread, peanut butter, fruit, and juice (KES 300–500 if self-prepared).
meals.dinner: Communal dinner at the lodge — grilled tilapia or chicken with rice and vegetables, around KES 800–1,100.

day_by_day.notes: Patience is key at the Mara River crossing — you may wait 1–3 hours for a crossing to happen. Bring plenty of water, a hat, and binoculars. Avoid making loud noises near the riverbank to not disturb the wildlife. Park entry fees are typically included in shared game drive packages — confirm this when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Morning nature walk with a certified Maasai guide along the lodge's surrounding conservancy area (outside the main park to avoid additional park fees). Learn about medicinal plants, animal tracks, and bird species. The Maasai Mara ecosystem hosts over 450 bird species — look for lilac-breasted rollers, secretary birds, and African fish eagles. Walk duration: 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mara Conservancy boundary areas which are often less crowded and more affordable than the core reserve. Hire a local guide for a budget walking safari (approx. KES 1,000–1,500). Observe wildlife including topi, eland, and Thomson's gazelles grazing on the open plains. Rest at the lodge during peak afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Maasai cultural performance at a nearby manyatta (homestead) if available — singing, jumping dances (adumu), and storytelling (approx. KES 500 per person). Return to the lodge for dinner and an early night to prepare for the next day's early start.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — mandazi, chai, scrambled eggs, and fresh fruit (KES 500–700 or included).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a budget local eatery near the lodge or self-catered with snacks — beans and chapati for around KES 250–400.
meals.dinner: Home-style dinner at the lodge or a local community kitchen if available — lentil soup, ugali, and sukuma wiki for around KES 600–900.

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris outside the national reserve boundaries are significantly cheaper than vehicle-based drives inside the park. Always walk with a certified guide for safety. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) to blend with the environment and avoid startling wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning shared game drive focusing on predator activity — lions and leopards are most active at dawn. Head toward the Talek River area or Musiara Marsh, known for large lion prides. The warm July weather (25°C highs) means animals congregate near water sources, making sightings more predictable. Spend 3–4 hours in the field.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge and spend the afternoon exploring the local area on foot. Visit a roadside curio market near the reserve gate to browse handmade Maasai jewelry, beaded items, and wooden carvings. Practice bargaining respectfully — prices can often be negotiated down by 30–50%. Budget KES 500–2,000 for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge with a sundowner drink (local Tusker beer or fresh passion juice — KES 150–300). Watch the spectacular African sunset paint the savannah in orange and red hues. Participate in a budget-friendly stargazing session — the Mara has minimal light pollution, offering stunning views of the Milky Way in July.

meals.breakfast: Pre-drive packed breakfast — hard-boiled eggs, bread, banana, and thermos tea (KES 400–600 or included).
meals.lunch: Budget lunch at the lodge or local duka (small shop) — rice and beans or chapati with fried egg for KES 200–400.
meals.dinner: Set dinner at the lodge — beef or chicken stew with ugali and a side salad, around KES 700–1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is a good mid-trip rest and cultural day. Avoid overspending at the curio market — set a budget before browsing. Stay hydrated throughout the day. Check with your lodge about any complimentary evening activities or talks by wildlife guides.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Oloololo (Siria) Escarpment area on the western edge of the Maasai Mara ecosystem. This dramatic landscape offers panoramic views over the reserve and Tanzania's Serengeti beyond. Arrange a shared vehicle or local transport (KES 500–1,000) to reach the escarpment viewpoint. Bring your camera — the views are breathtaking, especially in the clear July morning air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Birdwatching session near the Mara River or a seasonal wetland area. The Maasai Mara is a birding paradise — look for the grey crowned crane (Kenya's national bird), saddle-billed storks, and Verreaux's eagle owls. A local birding guide can be hired affordably (KES 800–1,200 for 2–3 hours). This is a great low-cost alternative to a full game drive.
day_by_day.evening: Community campfire and storytelling evening at the lodge or nearby Maasai homestead. Listen to local guides share wildlife tracking stories, Maasai legends, and conservation efforts in the Mara ecosystem. This is typically free or low-cost and provides authentic cultural immersion.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — porridge (uji), chai, and toast with local honey (KES 400–600 or included).
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the escarpment viewpoint — self-catered with packed sandwiches, fruit, and water (KES 300–500).
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at the lodge — vegetable curry with rice or chapati, around KES 650–900.

day_by_day.notes: The Oloololo Escarpment is best visited in the morning when visibility is clearest. Bring a light windbreaker as it can be breezy at higher elevations. The July rainfall (30mm average) may cause brief afternoon showers — carry a small rain poncho just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Mara North Conservancy or Naboisho Conservancy (adjacent to the main reserve). These community conservancies often have lower entry fees than the main national reserve and offer excellent, less-crowded wildlife viewing. Arrange a shared vehicle (KES 2,500–4,000 per person shared). Look for wild dogs, cheetahs, and large elephant herds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the conservancy. These areas allow walking safaris and night drives (not permitted in the main reserve), offering unique wildlife experiences at a budget-friendly price. Afternoon walking safari with a ranger (approx. KES 1,000–1,500 per person) through open grasslands.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your boutique stay by 18:00. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the lodge. Reflect on the week's wildlife highlights and organize your photos. Chat with your lodge hosts about any special sightings reported in the area for tomorrow's game drive.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast — fried eggs, sausage, toast, and chai (KES 500–700 or included).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch in the conservancy — self-catered or arranged through lodge (KES 400–600).
meals.dinner: Celebratory mid-trip dinner — treat yourself to a slightly upgraded meal at the lodge's main restaurant. Try nyama choma (roasted goat) with kachumbari (tomato-onion salsa) for around KES 1,000–1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Community conservancies directly support local Maasai communities through conservation fees — your visit has a positive impact. Always confirm conservancy entry fees in advance. Night drives in conservancies are a rare and special experience — ask your lodge if they can arrange one at a reasonable shared cost.

day_by_day.morning: Final dedicated game drive inside Maasai Mara National Reserve. Focus on areas you haven't fully explored — the Serena area or Keekorok plains. The Great Migration herds should be well established in the Mara by late July, offering spectacular scenes of thousands of wildebeest moving across the plains. Depart at 06:00 for maximum wildlife activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by noon. Spend the afternoon at a budget-friendly relaxation activity — read a wildlife book from the lodge library, sketch or journal your safari experiences, or simply sit quietly on the lodge veranda and observe the birdlife and any wildlife that wanders near the property. Many lodges in the Mara have resident warthogs, baboons, and impalas on their grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography session on the lodge grounds or a nearby open area with a guide. The July sky offers stunning golden-hour light over the savannah. Swap contact details with fellow travelers and share wildlife photos over drinks around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Pre-drive packed breakfast — fruit, boiled eggs, and thermos tea (KES 400–600 or included).
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch — tomato soup and bread, or a simple salad with grilled chicken (KES 500–800).
meals.dinner: Budget lodge dinner — fish fillet (tilapia) with chips and coleslaw or ugali with beef stew, around KES 800–1,100.

day_by_day.notes: Day 8 is your last full game drive day — make the most of it by communicating your target wildlife sightings to your driver-guide the night before. Tip your driver-guide appropriately at the end of your drives (KES 500–1,000 per day is customary and greatly appreciated on a budget tour).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the lodge — no game drive today. Take a slow breakfast and enjoy the lodge surroundings. Do a final birdwatching walk on the property. Pack and organize your belongings. Check out formalities and settle any outstanding bills. Take photos of the lodge, staff, and the beautiful Maasai Mara landscape as a farewell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey from Maasai Mara to Nairobi by shared shuttle or matatu (approx. KES 1,500–2,500). The 5–6 hour drive passes through Narok town — stop for a budget lunch break. Arrive in Nairobi by late afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in Nairobi (areas like Westlands or Kilimani have safe budget options for KES 1,500–3,000 per night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nairobi's budget-friendly attractions near your guesthouse. Visit a local market or take a walk through a safe neighborhood. Enjoy Nairobi's vibrant evening atmosphere. Try a local restaurant in the city for a change of cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — enjoy a full meal before the long journey (KES 500–700 or included).
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in Narok town — nyama choma, ugali, and sukuma wiki at a local eatery for KES 300–500.
meals.dinner: Nairobi budget restaurant dinner — try a local Kenyan restaurant for pilau rice, kachumbari, and chicken for KES 500–800. Nairobi has many affordable dining options.

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle back to Nairobi at least a day in advance to secure a seat. Store your main luggage at the lodge during your Mara stay if possible to travel lighter on game drives. Keep your valuables secure during the Nairobi arrival — stay alert in busy transport areas.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the final morning in Nairobi visiting budget-friendly attractions. Head to Nairobi National Park (entry approx. KES 2,000–3,000 for non-residents or KES 400 for residents) — the world's only national park within a capital city. Spot lions, rhinos, and giraffes with the city skyline in the background. Alternatively, visit the free David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage (donation-based, morning visiting hours 11:00–12:00) — a heartwarming wildlife conservation experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Giraffe Centre in Karen, Nairobi (entry approx. KES 1,500) to hand-feed endangered Rothschild giraffes — a memorable and affordable wildlife encounter. Afterward, explore the Karen Blixen Museum or browse the Maasai Market for last-minute affordable souvenirs (open on rotating days — check schedule). Head back to your guesthouse to collect luggage and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible 10-day budget safari adventure through the Maasai Mara. Enjoy a final cup of Kenyan chai at the airport — Kenya is one of the world's top tea producers and the airport cafés serve excellent brew for KES 100–200.

meals.breakfast: Budget guesthouse breakfast or local café near your accommodation — mandazi, chai, and scrambled eggs for KES 300–500.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Giraffe Centre or Karen area — try a local café for a sandwich and fresh juice for KES 400–700.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or final Nairobi restaurant dinner before departure — budget KES 600–1,000 for a satisfying last meal in Kenya.

day_by_day.notes: The David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage visiting hours are strictly 11:00–12:00 daily — plan accordingly. The Giraffe Centre is best visited in the afternoon when it is less crowded. Keep some Kenyan shillings for airport tips and last-minute purchases. Exchange any remaining KES back to your home currency at the airport bureau de change. Total estimated daily budget for activities, food, and local transport: KES 3,000–6,000 per day (approx. USD 20–40), excluding accommodation and major park fees.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer driver. Enjoy a scenic 5–6 hour drive southwest toward Maasai Mara National Reserve, passing through the Great Rift Valley escarpment with stunning viewpoints along the way. Stop at a roadside viewpoint near Narok town for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve as the golden hour light settles over the savanna. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome briefing from lodge staff about your stay and upcoming safari activities. Settle onto the lodge terrace for sundowner drinks while listening to the sounds of the African bush.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light snack box or quick bite at a café near the airport or en route at a clean roadside stop near Narok town (budget ~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique lodge – enjoy a set three-course African-inspired menu featuring dishes like nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali, and seasonal vegetables. Included or ~$25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your transfer pickup in advance. The Nairobi to Maasai Mara drive is approximately 270 km and takes 5–6 hours depending on road conditions. Carry light snacks and water for the journey. Arrive before darkness for safety on bush roads.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise at 05:30 for your first full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari game drive. Depart by 06:00 in an open 4x4 safari vehicle with your expert guide. Head toward the Mara River crossing zones where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles are actively migrating in July. Watch in awe as massive herds thunder across the plains and brave crocodile-filled river crossings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the central Mara plains searching for the Big Five – lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. Stop at a scenic picnic spot inside the reserve for a bush lunch provided by your lodge. Afternoon is prime time for big cat sightings as lions and cheetahs become active. Return to the lodge around 18:00.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a hot shower and relaxation. Gather around the campfire or lodge fire pit for storytelling with fellow travelers and your guide. Enjoy star-gazing in the remarkably clear Mara skies away from city light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at the lodge before departure – fresh fruit, eggs, toast, and coffee/tea (~included or $10–15).
meals.lunch: Packed bush picnic lunch provided by the lodge eaten in the field – sandwiches, fruit, juice boxes, and snacks.
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the lodge restaurant featuring East African cuisine – try the slow-cooked lamb stew with pilau rice and fresh kachumbari salad (~$25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season – river crossings are most frequent in the morning. Bring binoculars, a camera with zoom lens, sunscreen, and a warm layer for the early morning chill. Game drives typically run 06:00–13:00 and 15:30–18:30.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive departing at 06:00 focusing on the northern Mara Triangle area, known for dense wildlife concentrations during the migration. Look for large lion prides, hyena clans, and vast wildebeest columns stretching to the horizon. Your guide will track fresh animal prints and use radio communication with other guides to locate key sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by midday. After lunch, participate in the Maasai Cultural Village Experience – a guided visit to an authentic nearby Maasai boma (village). Meet the local Maasai community, participate in traditional jumping dances (adamu), learn about beadwork and crafts, and hear stories about Maasai warrior traditions and their coexistence with wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge by 18:00. Browse handcrafted Maasai souvenirs available at the village or lodge gift shop. Enjoy a relaxed sundowner on the lodge veranda overlooking the plains as the sun dips below the acacia-dotted horizon.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast buffet – fresh tropical fruits, yogurt, eggs to order, toast, and Kenyan chai tea (~included or $12–15).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge – light fare such as grilled tilapia, fresh salad, and lemonade (~$15–20).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge – enjoy a communal boma dinner (outdoor barbecue-style) with grilled meats, roasted vegetables, and traditional Kenyan sides under the stars (~$30–40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai Cultural Village Experience typically costs $20–40 per person and should be arranged through your lodge. Respect cultural protocols – ask before photographing community members and participate respectfully in all activities.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely morning with a guided nature walk around the lodge perimeter with a Maasai guide. Learn to identify local bird species (Kenya has over 1,000 bird species), track animal footprints, and discover medicinal plants used by the Maasai. This slower-paced activity offers an intimate connection with the bush environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon game drive (15:30–18:30) focusing on predator activity. Late afternoons in the Mara are excellent for spotting cheetahs hunting on open plains, leopards in acacia trees, and lions beginning their evening activity. Visit the Mara River banks to observe hippo pools and massive Nile crocodiles basking on the banks.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks in the field at a scenic elevated viewpoint arranged by your guide – a quintessential Kenya safari experience. Watch the spectacular African sunset paint the sky in shades of orange and purple over the endless Mara grasslands before returning to the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast – scrambled eggs, bacon, fresh juice, tropical fruit platter, and Kenyan coffee (~included or $12–15).
meals.lunch: Relaxed lunch at the lodge – enjoy a light soup and sandwich or African-style beef stew with chapati flatbread (~$15–18).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge restaurant – try the Kenyan coastal-inspired dish of coconut fish curry with basmati rice and fresh mango chutney (~$25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Nature walks require a certified Maasai guide for safety – arrange through your lodge the evening before. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) and closed-toe shoes. Carry insect repellent for evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (06:00) for a full-day excursion to Lake Nakuru National Park for the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Safari. The drive from Maasai Mara takes approximately 3–4 hours. En route, enjoy views of the Great Rift Valley floor and agricultural highlands. Arrive at Lake Nakuru by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring Lake Nakuru National Park. Witness thousands of lesser and greater flamingos painting the alkaline lake shoreline in vivid pink – one of Africa's most iconic wildlife spectacles. The park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos. Look for Rothschild's giraffes, baboons, waterbuck, and over 400 bird species. Enjoy a packed picnic lunch inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Lake Nakuru by 16:00 and begin the return drive toward Maasai Mara or overnight in a mid-range guesthouse near Nakuru town to break the journey. If staying near Nakuru, enjoy a relaxed dinner in town and rest for the next day's activities.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure – grab-and-go option with fruit, boiled eggs, and coffee (~included or $10).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch inside Lake Nakuru National Park – sandwiches, fruit, snacks, and water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Nakuru town or back at the Mara lodge – try Kenyan grilled chicken (kuku choma) with ugali and sukuma wiki (collard greens) (~$15–22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park entry fees apply (~$60 per person for non-residents). The flamingo population varies seasonally but July typically offers excellent sightings. Confirm rhino tracking zones with your guide upon arrival. This is a long driving day – depart no later than 06:00.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Maasai Mara if you overnighted near Nakuru, arriving by late morning. Alternatively, enjoy a rest morning at the lodge recovering from yesterday's long excursion day. Take advantage of the lodge's amenities – read on the veranda, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and watch wildlife from the lodge grounds (elephants and zebras often visit nearby water holes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive (15:00–18:30) in the southeastern Mara exploring the Talek River area. This region is excellent for elephant family herds, large buffalo groups, and diverse birdlife including the lilac-breasted roller, secretary bird, and African fish eagle. Your guide will share fascinating ecological insights about the Mara ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the lodge. Participate in an optional guided night sky astronomy session if offered by the lodge – the Mara's dark skies reveal the Milky Way in stunning clarity. Enjoy a nightcap at the lodge bar.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast buffet with fresh fruit, cereals, eggs, and Kenyan tea (~included or $12–15).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge – avocado salad, grilled cheese sandwich, and fresh passion fruit juice (~$12–18).
meals.dinner: Three-course lodge dinner – start with a vegetable soup, main of slow-braised beef short ribs with roasted sweet potatoes, and finish with a fresh fruit crumble dessert (~$28–38 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 6 is intentionally paced as a recovery and reflection day after the intensive Day 5 excursion. Use this day to review your wildlife photography, journal your experiences, and recharge for the final days of the safari.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a full-day road trip to Amboseli National Park for the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience. The drive from Maasai Mara to Amboseli takes approximately 4–5 hours via Narok and Nairobi bypass. Arrive at Amboseli by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enter Amboseli National Park and immediately begin game drives across the iconic swamp-dotted plains. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds – observe massive bulls, playful calves, and matriarch-led families up close against the breathtaking backdrop of snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro (Africa's highest peak at 5,895 m). The afternoon light on Kilimanjaro is spectacular for photography.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range tented camp or lodge near Amboseli. Enjoy sundowners with views of Kilimanjaro glowing pink in the alpenglow. The evening atmosphere in Amboseli is magical with elephant silhouettes moving across the plains at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure – packed option if leaving before 06:30 (~included).
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop en route or packed lunch from the Mara lodge – local restaurant serving chapati, beans, and tea (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Amboseli camp/lodge – enjoy East African-inspired cuisine with views of the darkening Kilimanjaro silhouette (~$25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli National Park entry fees apply (~$60 per person). Mount Kilimanjaro is most visible in the early morning and evening – clouds typically obscure the summit midday. Book Amboseli accommodation in advance as July is peak season. Dust can be heavy in Amboseli – bring a buff/scarf.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Amboseli (05:30–09:30) – this is the golden hour for Kilimanjaro views and elephant photography. Massive elephant herds emerge from the Ol Tukai swamp area at dawn, creating world-class wildlife photography opportunities. Also look for lions, cheetahs, zebras, wildebeest, and over 600 bird species including the African crowned crane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Observation Hill inside Amboseli for a panoramic 360-degree view of the entire park, swamps, and Kilimanjaro. Spend time at the swamp viewing area watching hippos, pelicans, and wading birds. Optional: visit the Amboseli Elephant Research Project information center to learn about decades of elephant behavioral research conducted here.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final Amboseli sundowner game drive as the golden light bathes the plains. Return to camp for a celebratory dinner reflecting on the incredible wildlife experiences of the past week. Share stories with fellow travelers around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field or full camp breakfast upon return – fresh fruit, eggs, toast, and Kenyan coffee (~included or $12–15).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp – light salad, grilled chicken wrap, and fresh juice (~$15–20).
meals.dinner: Special camp dinner – enjoy a candlelit outdoor dinner with grilled meats, African salads, and local desserts under the stars near Kilimanjaro (~$30–40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bring your best camera and longest zoom lens for Day 8 – the morning light on elephants with Kilimanjaro is one of the most photographed wildlife scenes in the world. Arrive at the swamp viewpoint by 06:00 for the best light and elephant activity.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Amboseli after an early breakfast and begin the drive back toward Nairobi (approximately 4 hours). En route, stop at the Aberdare Range foothills area for the Aberdare Forest Night Game Drive & Treetop Lodge experience. Check in to your Aberdare treetop-style lodge by early afternoon and explore the lodge's elevated viewing decks overlooking a floodlit waterhole.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into your unique treetop lodge accommodation and spend the afternoon watching wildlife arrive at the waterhole below – elephants, buffalos, giant forest hogs, and bushbuck are commonly seen. Take a short guided forest walk through the Aberdare highland rainforest discovering colobus monkeys, exotic orchids, and towering Podocarpus trees.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the highlight of the Aberdare stay – a nocturnal game drive through the Aberdare National Park after dark. With spotlights, your guide will reveal the secret nighttime world of leopards, servals, porcupines, genets, and the rare bongo antelope. Return to the treetop lodge and spend the night watching animals visit the floodlit waterhole from your room or viewing platform.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Amboseli camp before departure – eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee (~included).
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch en route or at the Aberdare lodge upon arrival – try a Kenyan staple of githeri (maize and bean stew) with fresh vegetables (~$10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Aberdare treetop lodge – highland-inspired cuisine featuring trout (farmed locally in Aberdare streams), roasted root vegetables, and fresh highland produce (~$28–38 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Aberdare National Park entry fees apply (~$52 per person). The night game drive typically departs around 19:00–21:00. Temperatures in the Aberdare highlands can drop to 10–15°C at night – pack a warm fleece or jacket. The treetop lodge experience is a classic Kenya tradition dating back to when Queen Elizabeth II learned she had become queen while staying at Treetops Lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aberdare treetop lodge – wake early to watch the dawn wildlife activity at the waterhole one last time. Enjoy a final full lodge breakfast with highland views. Pack your bags and begin the drive back to Nairobi (approximately 2.5–3 hours from the Aberdare area). Stop at a reputable curio market near Nairobi (such as the Maasai Market or Utamaduni Craft Centre) for last-minute souvenir shopping – Maasai beadwork, soapstone carvings, and Kenyan coffee make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nairobi by early afternoon. If time permits before your departure flight, visit the Nairobi Giraffe Centre (Rothschild's giraffes you can hand-feed, ~$15 entry) or the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage (free, donation-based, best visited 11:00–12:00). Transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Kenya safari adventure – the thundering Great Migration, elephant giants against Kilimanjaro, flamingo-painted lakes, Maasai cultural richness, and the mystical Aberdare forest nights.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast at the Aberdare treetop lodge – enjoy a leisurely final breakfast with highland views (~included or $12–15).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nairobi at a mid-range restaurant – try the Carnivore Restaurant (famous for game meats) or a local café serving nyama choma and Tusker beer (~$20–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining for your return journey.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at JKIA. Confirm your airport transfer is booked. Declare any wildlife products at customs – it is illegal to export items made from endangered species. Kenya requires a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate if arriving from certain countries – ensure your travel documents are in order.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds up close against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with iconic savannah landscapes and diverse birdlife.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Safari
experiences.description: Explore Lake Nakuru National Park, home to thousands of pink flamingos that paint the lake shores in vivid color. The park is also a sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and over 450 bird species, making it a compact but incredibly diverse wildlife destination.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the rich traditions of the Maasai people with an authentic village visit. Participate in traditional dances, learn about ancient warrior customs, visit local homesteads called manyattas, and shop for handcrafted beaded jewelry directly from artisans while gaining deep cultural insight into one of Africa's most iconic tribes.
experiences.location: Maasai Villages near Maasai Mara, Narok County

experiences.name: Aberdare Forest Night Game Drive & Treetop Lodge
experiences.description: Experience the magic of Kenya's highland rainforest with a nocturnal game drive through the Aberdare National Park. Spot elusive forest elephants, giant forest hogs, bongos, and leopards by spotlight. Staying at a treetop lodge over a waterhole allows you to watch wildlife gather through the night in a truly unique setting.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, a dedicated luxury concierge and private transfer await you at the arrivals hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury charter flight or premium road transfer from Nairobi to the Maasai Mara (approximately 45 minutes by air or 5–6 hours by road). Settle into your boutique lodge in the Maasai Mara National Reserve, enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal safari guide. Take a short, leisurely sunset game drive around the lodge perimeter to acclimatize and spot resident wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive bush sundowner on a scenic kopje overlooking the savannah — sip premium Kenyan gin and tonics while watching the golden sunset. Return to the lodge for a private welcome dinner under the stars around a traditional boma fire.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge dining prior to arrival)
meals.lunch: Light gourmet welcome spread at the lodge upon check-in — artisan charcuterie, fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan cheeses, and freshly brewed safari tea
meals.dinner: Private boma dinner featuring slow-roasted Maasai lamb, grilled seasonal vegetables, ugali, and a curated selection of South African and Kenyan wines

day_by_day.notes: Pack a light fleece for the evening game drive — temperatures can drop to around 15°C after sunset in the Mara. Ensure your camera batteries are fully charged for the sunset drive.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day Great Migration Safari — depart at dawn (06:00) for prime positioning at the Mara River crossing points. Witness the spectacular Great Migration as millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles thunder across the plains in one of nature's greatest wildlife spectacles. Your private guide will navigate to the best vantage points.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration Safari along the Mara River banks. Enjoy a gourmet bush picnic lunch served by your lodge butler in the field. Afternoon game drives through the open savannah tracking lion prides, cheetah, leopard, and the Big Five in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a relaxing outdoor spa treatment — signature Maasai hot stone massage using locally sourced oils. Freshen up and enjoy cocktails at the lodge's elevated viewing deck before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full English safari breakfast at the lodge — farm eggs, smoked bacon, fresh Kenyan sausages, grilled tomatoes, and freshly squeezed passion fruit juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic in the Mara — smoked salmon wraps, quinoa salad, artisan bread, chilled gazpacho, and sparkling water served on linen-draped tables in the field
meals.dinner: Five-course fine dining at the lodge's signature restaurant — cream of wild mushroom soup, pan-seared Nile perch, Maasai-spiced beef tenderloin, Kenyan cheese board, and dark chocolate fondant with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are most likely in the morning. Bring high-SPF sunscreen and a wide-brimmed hat. Binoculars are essential for spotting wildlife across the vast plains.

day_by_day.morning: Hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise — float silently above the golden savannah as herds of wildebeest and zebra move below you. This exclusive experience offers a breathtaking bird's-eye perspective of the migration and the sweeping Mara landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Cultural Village Experience — visit an authentic Maasai enkang (homestead) accompanied by a knowledgeable cultural guide. Participate in traditional jumping dances (adumu), learn about Maasai beadwork, herbal medicine, and cattle culture. Meet village elders and women artisans, and purchase handcrafted souvenirs directly supporting the community.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner game drive along the Mara River followed by a private candlelit dinner set up in the bush — a truly magical al fresco dining experience under a canopy of stars with the sounds of the African night surrounding you.

meals.breakfast: Traditional champagne breakfast in the bush following the balloon landing — chilled Moët & Chandon, smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, fresh pastries, and tropical fruit platters served on linen-draped tables
meals.lunch: Traditional Maasai-inspired lunch at the cultural village — fermented milk (mursik), roasted goat meat, mukimo (mashed potato and greens), and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Private bush dinner — grilled lobster thermidor, Kenyan-spiced rack of lamb, roasted root vegetables, and a sommelier-curated wine pairing from South Africa's Stellenbosch region

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon safari requires an early wake-up (typically 04:30–05:00). Book in advance as spaces are extremely limited. Wear layers as balloon flights can be cool at altitude. The Maasai village visit is a genuine community initiative — tips and purchases go directly to the village.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided walking safari in the Maasai Mara conservancy with an expert Maasai tracker — experience the bush at ground level, tracking animal footprints, identifying medicinal plants, insects, and birds invisible from a vehicle. This intimate experience offers a completely different perspective of the ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Photography masterclass game drive with a professional wildlife photographer guide — learn composition techniques, lighting tricks, and animal behavior reading while capturing stunning images of the Mara's incredible wildlife. Focus on big cats, which are especially active in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner hosted at a remote tented camp set up beside the Mara River — ambient lantern lighting, a private chef, and the gentle sounds of hippos in the water create an unforgettable atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the lodge — freshly baked croissants, Kenyan single-origin coffee, Greek yogurt with local honey, granola, and a tropical fruit platter
meals.lunch: Gourmet lodge lunch — prawn and avocado salad, grilled Nile perch with lemon butter, fresh chapati, and a selection of Kenyan craft sodas and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Riverside private dining — wood-fired whole sea bass, truffle-infused risotto, roasted asparagus, and a decadent passion fruit cheesecake for dessert, paired with premium Burgundy wines

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris require closed-toe shoes and neutral-colored clothing. Always stay with your armed Maasai guide. The photography drive is best in late afternoon (golden hour) — bring extra memory cards and a telephoto lens if available.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the Maasai Mara early for a private charter flight to Amboseli National Park (approximately 1 hour). Check into your luxury lodge with iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience — observe some of Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds roaming the swamps and open plains against the dramatic backdrop of Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue elephant watching with a private naturalist guide — Amboseli is renowned for its large matriarchal elephant families. Visit the Amboseli Research Centre to learn about long-term elephant conservation research. Late afternoon game drive spotting buffalo, lions, cheetah, and hundreds of bird species.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at a private lookout point with unobstructed views of Kilimanjaro bathed in the last golden light of the day. Return to the lodge for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Full safari breakfast at the Mara lodge before departure — eggs to order, fresh tropical juices, Kenyan tea, pastries, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Amboseli lodge — chilled cucumber gazpacho, grilled chicken with Kenyan spices, seasonal vegetable tagine, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Elegant lodge dinner with Kilimanjaro moonrise views — pan-roasted duck breast, wild mushroom risotto, roasted beet salad, and a warm chocolate lava cake with Kenyan coffee ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli can be dusty — bring a buff or light scarf to cover your face during game drives. July mornings offer the best Kilimanjaro views before clouds build. The elephant herds are most active near the swamps in the morning and late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day immersive Amboseli elephant experience — early morning game drive to the Enkongo Narok swamp where elephant herds gather in the thousands. Watch bulls sparring, calves playing, and matriarchs leading their families through the papyrus marshes. Kilimanjaro provides a stunning snow-capped backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a Maasai community conservation area bordering Amboseli — learn about human-wildlife coexistence programs and how Maasai communities benefit from conservation. Participate in a traditional bead-making workshop with Maasai women artisans. Late afternoon game drive back through the park.
day_by_day.evening: Private star-gazing experience with an expert astronomer guide — Amboseli's remote location and clear July skies offer extraordinary visibility of the Milky Way and Southern Cross. Premium telescopes provided. Followed by a nightcap at the lodge fire.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field beside the swamp — French press Kenyan coffee, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and fresh pastries with a front-row view of elephants
meals.lunch: Luxury picnic in the Amboseli plains — prosciutto and fig crostini, grilled vegetable antipasto, artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Seven-course tasting menu at the lodge's fine dining pavilion — featuring locally sourced Kenyan ingredients: Mombasa prawns, Rift Valley lamb, highland trout, and a Kenyan coffee and chocolate dessert flight

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's elephant population is one of the most studied in the world — your guide can identify individual elephants by name. Bring polarized sunglasses to reduce glare from the alkaline dust. Star-gazing sessions typically begin at 20:30.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Lake Nakuru (approximately 1.5 hours). Check into a luxury lodge on the lake's edge. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Safari — explore Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to thousands of lesser and greater flamingos that paint the alkaline lake shores in vivid pink.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dedicated rhino tracking experience with an expert guide — Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's premier sanctuaries for both black and white rhino. Track these critically endangered animals on foot (within safe parameters) and by vehicle. Also spot Rothschild's giraffe, waterbuck, and cape buffalo.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the escarpment viewpoint overlooking the entire lake — watch the flamingo flocks shift and swirl in the golden light. Return to the lodge for a relaxing spa session.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before departure — eggs to order, fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan tea and coffee, pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Lake Nakuru lodge — roasted pepper soup, grilled lake trout with lemon caper butter, seasonal vegetables, and freshly baked bread
meals.dinner: Lakeside dinner with flamingo views — slow-braised Kenyan beef short rib, truffle mashed potato, wilted spinach with garlic, and a passion fruit and mango pavlova

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo numbers vary seasonally — July typically offers excellent viewing. Rhino tracking requires patience and silence; follow your guide's instructions at all times. The escarpment viewpoint is best visited 30–45 minutes before sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat safari on Lake Nakuru — glide silently through the flamingo flocks at water level for extraordinary photography opportunities. Spot pelicans, cormorants, African fish eagles, and hippos in the shallows. The morning light creates magical pink reflections on the alkaline water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Aberdare Forest region (approximately 2.5 hours from Lake Nakuru) — check into a luxury treetop lodge built above a floodlit waterhole in the Aberdare National Park. Afternoon game viewing from your private treehouse balcony as wildlife gathers at the waterhole below.
day_by_day.evening: Aberdare Forest Night Game Drive — experience the magic of Kenya's highland rainforest with a nocturnal game drive. Spot elusive forest creatures including bongo antelope, giant forest hog, leopard, hyena, and bushbuck illuminated by spotlights. Return to the treetop lodge for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast on the lodge terrace overlooking Lake Nakuru — smoked salmon bagels, fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, Kenyan single-origin pour-over coffee, and freshly squeezed pink grapefruit juice
meals.lunch: En route picnic lunch at a scenic highland viewpoint — gourmet sandwiches, antipasto board, fresh fruit, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at the treetop lodge with live waterhole viewing — highland trout fillet, Aberdare mushroom and truffle pasta, roasted root vegetables, and a warm sticky toffee pudding with cream

day_by_day.notes: The night game drive requires warm layers — Aberdare temperatures can drop to 10°C at night. Red-filter torches are provided to avoid disturbing nocturnal animals. Keep noise to a minimum during the night drive for the best wildlife sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for the most magical experience at the Aberdare treetop lodge — the floodlit waterhole comes alive as elephant herds, buffalo, and rhino visit in the early hours. Watch from your private balcony with hot Kenyan coffee in hand. Morning guided forest walk with a Kikuyu tracker to discover the incredible biodiversity of the Aberdare ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight back to Nairobi (approximately 45 minutes). Check into a luxury five-star hotel in Nairobi (Hemingways, The Fairmont Norfolk, or similar). Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the hotel's world-class spa, swimming pool, and manicured gardens. Optional visit to the nearby Giraffe Centre or David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail reception at the hotel's rooftop bar with panoramic Nairobi skyline views. Private farewell dinner at Nairobi's finest restaurant — a celebration of an extraordinary Kenyan journey.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn continental spread at the treetop lodge — freshly brewed highland coffee, pastries, granola, and fresh fruit enjoyed while watching wildlife at the waterhole
meals.lunch: Gourmet welcome lunch at the Nairobi luxury hotel — chilled avocado and prawn salad, grilled chicken with Kenyan spices, fresh chapati, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Farewell fine dining experience at Carnivore Restaurant or The Talisman, Nairobi — a multi-course celebration dinner featuring the finest Kenyan and East African cuisine, paired with premium wines and ending with a Kenyan coffee and petit fours

day_by_day.notes: The Giraffe Centre and Elephant Orphanage are both within 20–30 minutes of central Nairobi — book in advance as they are popular. Nairobi's altitude (1,795m) means evenings are pleasantly cool — bring a light jacket for the rooftop bar.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Nairobi — enjoy a luxurious lie-in followed by a full breakfast at the hotel. Optional last-minute luxury shopping at the Westgate Mall or Village Market for premium Kenyan crafts, coffee, teas, and souvenirs. Visit the Karen Blixen Museum in the leafy Karen suburb for a cultural and historical perspective on Kenya's colonial past.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport with your dedicated concierge. VIP airport lounge access arranged for a comfortable pre-departure experience. Enjoy Kenyan tea, snacks, and Wi-Fi in the exclusive lounge while reflecting on an extraordinary 10-day Kenyan adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi — carry the memories of the Great Migration, elephant herds beneath Kilimanjaro, pink flamingo lakes, and starlit African nights home with you.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the Nairobi hotel — a full buffet spread featuring Kenyan specialties including mandazi (sweet fried dough), chai tea, fresh tropical fruits, eggs to order, smoked meats, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel or Karen restaurant — avocado on sourdough, grilled Nile perch tacos, and a final glass of chilled Kenyan craft beer or passion fruit juice
meals.dinner: Airport VIP lounge dining or in-flight premium dining on your homeward journey

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in at JKIA. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no ivory, live animals, or uncertified animal products. Kenyan single-origin coffee and loose-leaf tea make excellent duty-free gifts. Your concierge can assist with any last-minute packing or logistics.
